### rental_ext_repair_customer_discount (agent tool)
- Hub "Repair-Customer Discount Credit on Customer-Pay Rentals": rule sentence, tool contract (matches docstring).
- **Prerequisite → rental_ext_time_charge_correction (form state).** policy_source "The repair-customer discount is worked out only after any amount by which the time charge was posted above the rental's correct time charge stands credited against it as a billing error." It appears verbatim in this hub (2nd paragraph), and a whole-corpus string search finds it in no other document. Connective "only after", strength (hard gate) and state form are intact. Resolution basis: the depended-on hub describes in the same words the write that brings the state about ("corrects the time charge … above the time charge the rental should carry … booked … as a customer credit with reason billing error"); the records (`find_rental_ledger` time charge 773.82/18 days, no billing_error credit) plus the correction computation show the state is unmet. The depended-on docs do not carry the blocked side's sentence. `condition`/`resolved_by` have no home in prose ✓.
- Baseline → "Repair-Customer Discount: Amount of the Credit": the class customer-pay percent of the posted time charge, rounded to the cent, with the source (class rate schedule) named. Complete; nothing added; no hint.
- Factors: discount_base_choice → "Discount Base of the … Repair-Customer Discount" (corrected invoice / final − billing-error credits / final; full ladder). repair_period_share → "Repair-Period Share" (released + returned after → by release date; not released but ready → by ready date; else one; full ladder). overrun_discount_rate → "Discount Rate for Customer-Pay Repair Overruns" (>3 → double; 1–3 → +5; none → class percent; full ladder; reads "target turnaround … under Customer-Pay Repairs"). calibration_points (cross_difficulty adas) → "Calibration Department Points Table" (failed + sublet 5; failed, no sublet 2; else 0; full ladder, names ADAS Sensor Calibrations). program_points → "Repair Programme Points" (returning → tier returning-customer %; military → tier military %; else 0).
- Assembly "base × repair-period share × (rate + calibration points + program points) / 100, rounded once": carried across the factor docs ("the discount is given on that share of the discount base"; "percentage points added to the credit's discount rate" in both points docs; "the discount base, being the amount … on which the … credit is given"). The baseline doc carries "rounded to the cent once at the end". Equivalent at the level of entailment; the blind derivation reached exactly this assembly.
- Overwrite: settlement_split "with a customer_pay_discount credit of customer_pay_discount_pct percent …" → "Settlement Statement Notes" lists it as "no longer in force" ✓.

### rental_ext_delay_goodwill (on_request; user tool)
- Hub "Delay Goodwill Credit for Held-Up Customer-Pay Repairs": request sentence, desk offers / customer accepts, names the time charge, goodwill reason. The user-owned tool contract matches the docstring.
- **Prerequisite → rental_ext_repair_customer_discount (state).** "A goodwill credit for lost rental days is not fixed until the repair-customer discount owed on the time charge stands against it." Verbatim in this hub only; the connective "not … until", strength and state form are intact. Resolution: the depended-on hub describes the write in the same words ("repair-customer discount credit that names the rental's time charge and is booked on the rental"), and the ledger shows no customer_pay_discount credit.
- **Prerequisite → rental_ext_young_renter_fee (state).** "The goodwill credit for lost rental days is fixed only after every young-renter fee the renter owes on the rental stands as a charge on it." Verbatim in this hub only; intact. Resolution: "Young-Renter Charge on the Final Invoice" describes the posting, the class spec sheet gives the highest age 24 against `renter_age` 22, and the ledger has no young_renter charge.
- Baseline → "Computation Note: Amount of the … Delay Goodwill Credit": the standard credited days (business-day overrun capped at class authority days), day value (posted − all credits)/posted days + lost-day fee value, 0.5 share, lost-day fee value definition, rental days. It also carries the caps and the final rounding ("never more than the class goodwill credit authority days at the class partner daily rate less goodwill already credited … never more than the time charge still standing …; never below zero … rounded … once at the end"). These come from the extended rule's assembly sentence, with the authority days at their baseline value. They are source semantics, not an addition, and the doc gives no hint of variation. Default constants (class authority 1 day via the desk authority table, 0.5) are present.
- Factors: calibration_delay_days (cross adas) → "Calibration Department Measure: Delay Days" (failed + sublet → first attempt..completion; failed then passed → first..passing; else business-day overrun; full ladder). goodwill_authority_tier (cross warranty) → "Desk Authority Table" (sublet & active warranty 3; exactly one 2; else class authority 1; carries both uses of the authority days). lost_day_time_basis → "Lost-Day Time Value" (billing-error credit → /rental days; else corrected → /its days; else /posted days; "every standing credit" defined). delay_goodwill_share → "Delay Goodwill Share by Overrun and Dealer Sublet" (>3 & sublet 1.0; exactly one 0.75; else 0.5). program_uplift → "Repair Programme Uplift" (military, returning-customer, else 0; × (100 + uplift)/100; "the limits on the credit apply to the uplifted figure"). All ladders full. Thresholds are given in figures in each document.
- Overwrites: customer_settlement goodwill cap clause → "Customer Account Terms" "no longer in force" ✓. rental_days grace clause ✓ (above).

### Policy-side notes (do not change this skill's verdict)
1. Parameter description vs retired clause (goodwill). `parameter_schema.goodwill_credit_authority_days` reads "Most the desk may credit as goodwill on one rental, in rental days at the class's partner rate". The KB renders it faithfully in "Desk Authority and Service Limits" ("the desk may credit as goodwill on one rental at most 1 rental day at the class's partner rate"). After the overwrite of the base cap clause, the extended policy lets the cap rise to 3 authority days; task 0's GT 82.21 exceeds 42.99. The visible corpus settles it (the authority table rule, and "no longer in force" on the old cap), but the parameter description still reads as an absolute cap. This is an inconsistency on the policy side; the documents translate it faithfully.
2. Parameter description vs retired clause (return grace). `parameter_schema.return_grace_minutes` ("Minutes past the end of a rental day within which a return does not start a further rental day") repeats the semantics of the retired grace clause. The KB renders it in "Rental Day, Return, Fuel and Mileage Terms" (Return grace 29 minutes), while "Rental Days, Returns and Covered Days Used" marks the clause no longer in force. It does not affect task 0 (return 07:30 is before the 08:10 pickup time). Same nature as note 1.
3. Tool-side: the contracts say "rounded half-up", the implementations use Python `round(float, 2)`. No effect on these GT values.
